newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sets $70 mln minimum bid for La Oroya - source.
newsitem.headline: Peru sets $70 mln minimum bid for La Oroya - source.

text.p: Peru's state miner Centromin has set a $70 million minimum bid price for the April 14 auction of its huge La Oroya metallurgic complex, a company source said Tuesday.
The winning bidder will also be obliged to invest over the next five years $120 million in the smelting and refining complex that processes 22 metals and their byproducts, the source added.

Under the terms of the privatization, the winning bidder will form a special company as the new owner of the complex and immediately inject the money offered at the auction into this new firm as capital, Centromin officials said.

Doe Run Co of the United States and Mexico's Industrias Penoles S.A. are interested in acquiring the smelting and refining complex, located in Peru's central Andes 120 miles (190 km) east of Lima at an altitude of 3,700 metres above sea level, according to Centromin.
As part of its piecemeal privatization, Centromin hopes to follow the La Oroya sale with the auction of a 100 percent stake in its San Cristobal and Andaychagua mines as one asset.
The government also plans to sell Centromin's remaining mines, a railroad network, port facilities, four hydroelectric plants and several prospects by the middle of 1997.
